name: Ted Dabney
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Atari in 1971 at age 34; no material milestone by age 26 found. By 26 (c.1963), Dabney was working as an engineer at Ampex after serving in the Marine Corps and briefly attending San Francisco State University.
early_history_summary: Dabney grew up in San Francisco, studied electronics in the Marine Corps, and worked at Bank of America before joining Ampex as a video circuit designer. He met Nolan Bushnell at Ampex and they later co-founded Syzygy/Atari in 1971, when Dabney was 34.
family_context_summary: Parents divorced when young; raised by father in San Francisco. Not documented in reviewed sources beyond this.
evidence_summary: Dabney's material milestone (co-founding Atari and co-creating Computer Space) occurred in 1971 when he was 34, well beyond age 26. By 26, he was an early-career engineer with no notable product, publication, or company founding. No material milestone by age 26 found.

name: Dennis Ritchie
milestone_by_age_26: Created C language in 1972 at age 31 and co-created Unix in 1969 at age 28; no material milestone by age 26 found. By 26 (1967), Ritchie had just joined Bell Labs and was beginning work on Multics after completing graduate studies at Harvard.
early_history_summary: Ritchie graduated from Harvard with a BS in Physics (1963) and was a graduate student in applied mathematics, working part-time at MIT Project MAC on Multics. He joined Bell Labs in 1967 at age 26, where he later co-created Unix with Ken Thompson and created the C programming language.
family_context_summary: Father Alistair E. Ritchie was a longtime Bell Labs scientist and co-author of The Design of Switching Circuits. Dennis grew up in Summit, New Jersey.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a Bell Labs scientist who co-authored an influential book on switching circuit theory, providing direct domain proximity in computing and electronics.
evidence_summary: Ritchie's seminal achievements (Unix in 1969 at age 28, C in 1972 at age 31) came after age 26. By 26, he had joined Bell Labs and was working on Multics, but had not yet produced a notable publication, product, or discovery. His father's Bell Labs career provided domain proximity but no material milestone was achieved by age 26.

name: Trae Stephens
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. The selection note 'Co-founded Founders Fund at 26' is incorrect; Founders Fund was founded by Peter Thiel in 2005. Stephens joined as a partner in 2014 and co-founded Anduril in 2017. By 26 (c.2011), Stephens was an early employee at Palantir Technologies, not a founder.
early_history_summary: Stephens grew up in Lebanon, Ohio, graduated from Georgetown's School of Foreign Service in 2005, worked as a computational linguist in the US Intelligence Community, then joined Palantir Technologies in 2008 as an early employee. He later joined Founders Fund as a partner in 2014 and co-founded Anduril Industries in 2017.
evidence_summary: Stephens did not co-found Founders Fund (founded by Thiel in 2005) nor achieve a material milestone by age 26. By 26, he was an early Palantir employee, which is notable employment but not a founding, product launch, seminal publication, or commercial success in his own right. His material milestones (Founders Fund partner in 2014, Anduril co-founder in 2017) came later.

name: David Filo
milestone_by_age_26: Co-created Yahoo directory in February 1994 at age 27 and co-founded Yahoo! Inc. in April 1995 at age 29; no material milestone by age 26 found. By 26 (April 1992), Filo was a Stanford PhD student in electrical engineering with an MS degree.
early_history_summary: Filo grew up in Moss Bluff, Louisiana, earned a BS in computer engineering from Tulane University, and an MS in electrical engineering from Stanford in 1990. He was a PhD student at Stanford when he and Jerry Yang created 'Jerry and David's Guide to the World Wide Web' in February 1994, which became Yahoo!.
family_context_summary: Born in Wisconsin, raised in Moss Bluff, Louisiana. Attended Tulane on a Dean's Honor Scholarship. Not documented in reviewed sources beyond this.
evidence_summary: Filo's material milestone (co-creating Yahoo with Jerry Yang) occurred in 1994 when he was 27, just after age 26. By 26, he was a Stanford PhD student with no notable product, publication, or company. The Yahoo directory and Yahoo! Inc. were both founded after age 26.

name: Claude Shannon
milestone_by_age_26: Published seminal master's thesis 'A Symbolic Analysis of Relay and Switching Circuits' in 1938 at age 22, applying Boolean algebra to switching circuit design and founding the field of digital circuit design; won the Alfred Noble Prize for this work in 1940 at age 24.
early_history_summary: Shannon graduated from the University of Michigan with dual degrees in mathematics and electrical engineering at age 20, then went to MIT where he worked on Vannevar Bush's differential analyzer and wrote his groundbreaking master's thesis applying Boolean algebra to relay switching circuits. The thesis, published in 1938, was called 'the most important master's thesis of the century' and won the Alfred Noble Prize in 1940. He completed his PhD in mathematics at MIT in 1940 and joined Bell Labs in 1941.
family_context_summary: Born in Petoskey and raised in Gaylord, Michigan (pop. ~3000), the son of a businessman/probate judge and a high school principal. His father was clever mathematically and gave him radio sets to tinker with; his paternal grandfather was a farmer and inventor with a washing machine patent. A distant relative of Thomas Edison. He built model planes, radio circuits, a radio-controlled boat, and a barbed-wire telegraph to a friend's house as a youth.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a businessman and probate judge who was mathematically inclined and provided radio sets; mother was a language teacher and high school principal; paternal grandfather was an inventor with a patent. No direct family background in engineering or computing, but a culture of tinkering and mathematical interest.
primary_early_advantage_tags: elite institution, MIT, Bell Labs, Vannevar Bush, differential analyzer, Boolean algebra, Alfred Noble Prize
evidence_summary: Shannon graduated from the University of Michigan at 20 with dual degrees in math and EE, then went to MIT where he worked on Vannevar Bush's differential analyzer and wrote a groundbreaking master's thesis (1938, age 22) applying Boolean algebra to switching circuits, founding digital circuit design. He won the Alfred Noble Prize in 1940 for this work, well before age 26. His father was a businessman/probate judge who was mathematically inclined and provided radio sets; his grandfather was an inventor. He benefited from elite institutional pipelines (Michigan, MIT, Bell Labs) and mentorship under Vannevar Bush, but no significant family financial advantage or direct tech-domain inheritance is documented. His scarce intellectual depth in applying mathematical logic to engineering problems was the primary leverage engine.

name: Nolan Bushnell
milestone_by_age_26: Founded Atari in 1972 at age 29 and created Computer Space in 1970 at age 27; no material milestone by age 26 found. By 26 (February 1969), Bushnell was working as an engineer at Ampex Corporation after graduating from the University of Utah in 1968.
early_history_summary: Bushnell grew up in Clearfield, Utah, worked at Lagoon Amusement Park during college, and graduated from the University of Utah with a BS in electrical engineering in 1968. He then worked at Ampex, where he met Ted Dabney. They co-founded Syzygy (later Atari) in 1970 and created Computer Space, the first commercial arcade video game.
family_context_summary: Born in Clearfield, Utah, to a middle-class LDS family. His father died when he was 15, and he took over the family concrete business. Not documented in reviewed sources beyond this.
evidence_summary: Bushnell's material milestones (Computer Space in 1970 at age 27, founding Atari in 1972 at age 29) came after age 26. By 26, he was a recent graduate working as an engineer at Ampex with no notable product, publication, or company founding. His amusement park experience provided domain exposure but no material milestone was achieved by age 26.

name: Gabe Newell
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Valve in 1996 at age 34 and shipped Half-Life in 1998 at age 36; no material milestone by age 26 found. By 26 (November 1988), Newell was a Microsoft employee who had contributed to Windows 1.0 (1985) and Windows 2.0 (1987) as a program manager, but neither was a breakout commercial success and he was not a founder.
early_history_summary: Newell grew up in Davis, California, attended Harvard University in 1980, and dropped out to join Microsoft in 1983 after being encouraged by Steve Ballmer. He spent 13 years at Microsoft as a programmer and program manager, working on the first three releases of Windows. He co-founded Valve with Mike Harrington in 1996 and shipped Half-Life in 1998.
family_context_summary: Born in Aspen, Colorado, grew up in Davis, California. Attended Harvard University but dropped out. Not documented in reviewed sources beyond this.
evidence_summary: Newell's material milestones (co-founding Valve in 1996 at 34, Half-Life in 1998 at 36, Steam in 2003) all came well after age 26. By 26, he was a Microsoft employee contributing to Windows 1.0 and 2.0, which were not commercially successful products. While he gained valuable experience at Microsoft, no independently verifiable material milestone (founding, seminal product, major prize, commercial success) was achieved by age 26.

name: Adam D'Angelo
milestone_by_age_26: Became Chief Technology Officer of Facebook in 2006 at age 22, then co-founded Quora in June 2009 at age 24, both before age 26.
early_history_summary: D'Angelo attended Phillips Exeter Academy where he developed the Synapse Media Player with Mark Zuckerberg. He studied computer science at Caltech (2002-2006) while competing at the highest levels of competitive programming (IOI silver medal 2002, ICPC world finalist). He joined Facebook in 2004 as one of its earliest engineers, became CTO in 2006, and co-founded Quora with Charlie Cheever in June 2009.
family_context_summary: Born in Redding, Connecticut. Attended Phillips Exeter Academy, an elite boarding school, suggesting family resources and emphasis on education. Family financial background is not otherwise documented.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Phillips Exeter, Caltech, competitive programming, IOI silver medal, Zuckerberg, Facebook, ICPC, Silicon Valley
evidence_summary: D'Angelo attended Phillips Exeter Academy where he developed Synapse with Zuckerberg, then studied CS at Caltech while achieving elite competitive programming results (IOI silver medal, ICPC world finalist). He joined Facebook in 2004, became CTO at 22 in 2006, and co-founded Quora at 24 in 2009, all before age 26. His family background is not well documented, but attendance at Phillips Exeter suggests family resources. His primary leverage was scarce technical depth amplified by elite institutional networks (Exeter, Caltech, Facebook) and a high-trust peer relationship with Zuckerberg that opened the Facebook door.

name: Sara Mauskopf
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Winnie in 2016 at age 31; no material milestone by age 26 found. By 26 (c.2011), Mauskopf was a product manager at Twitter, having previously worked at Google and YouTube. She was an employee, not a founder, with no notable product or publication to her name.
early_history_summary: Mauskopf graduated from MIT with a computer science degree and worked in product management at Google, YouTube, Twitter (approximately 4 years), and Postmates (Director of Product from 2014) before co-founding Winnie, a childcare marketplace, in 2016 with Anne Halsall.
evidence_summary: Mauskopf's material milestone (co-founding Winnie in 2016 at age 31) came well after age 26. By 26, she was a product manager at Twitter with no founding, notable product, publication, or commercial success in her own right. Her career at Google, YouTube, and Twitter provided valuable experience but no independently verifiable material milestone by age 26.

name: Aaron Swartz
milestone_by_age_26: Co-authored the RSS 1.0 specification at age 14 in 2000, became co-owner of Reddit through the Infogami merger in 2005 at age 19, and Reddit was acquired by Conde Nast in 2006 for approximately $5 million at age 20, all well before age 26.
early_history_summary: Swartz was immersed in computing from a young age, creating an encyclopedia website at 12 that won the ArsDigita Prize, and co-authoring the RSS 1.0 specification at 14. He became involved with Creative Commons at 15, enrolled at Stanford in 2004 but left after one year, founded Infogami (which merged with Reddit in 2005), and became a co-owner of Reddit. He also created the web.py framework and helped define Markdown syntax.
family_context_summary: Born in Highland Park, Illinois, to a Jewish family. Father Robert Swartz founded the software firm Mark Williams Company. Attended North Shore Country Day School, a private school near Chicago. Left high school after ninth grade to take courses at Lake Forest College.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father founded and ran the Mark Williams Company, a software firm, providing direct domain exposure to software entrepreneurship from an early age. The family was comfortable enough to send him to private school.
primary_early_advantage_tags: father software company, early internet, RSS 1.0, Reddit, W3C, Creative Commons, ArsDigita Prize, web.py, Markdown
evidence_summary: Swartz was immersed in computing from a very young age, creating an encyclopedia website at 12 (winning the ArsDigita Prize) and co-authoring the RSS 1.0 specification at 14. His father founded the software firm Mark Williams Company, providing direct domain exposure, and he attended a private school in suburban Chicago. He founded Infogami, which merged with Reddit in 2005 at age 19, making him a co-owner; Reddit was acquired by Conde Nast in 2006 for approximately $5 million. He was deeply embedded in early internet communities and the W3C/Creative Commons ecosystem, which provided both technical depth and distribution channels. His primary leverage was early specialization and platform-native compounding through internet communities, catalyzed by his father's software background.

name: Roelof Botha
milestone_by_age_26: Joined PayPal in 2000 at age 27, became CFO in September 2001 at age 28, and led PayPal's IPO in February 2002 at age 28; no material milestone by age 26 found. By 26 (September 1999), Botha was an MBA student at Stanford Graduate School of Business.
early_history_summary: Botha grew up in Cape Town, South Africa, earned a BSc in Actuarial Science from the University of Cape Town in 1996 (with the best GPA in university history), worked at McKinsey in Johannesburg from 1996-1998, then moved to the US for an MBA at Stanford. He joined PayPal in 2000 as director of corporate development, became CFO in 2001, and led the IPO in 2002 before joining Sequoia Capital in 2003.
family_context_summary: Born in Pretoria, South Africa; grandfather was Pik Botha, South Africa's foreign minister during the apartheid era. Moved to Cape Town at age six. Raised in Hout Bay, a suburb of Cape Town.
parent_family_domain_summary: Grandfather Pik Botha was a prominent political figure (foreign minister of South Africa), providing high-status family networks but not in the technology domain.
evidence_summary: Botha's material milestones (joining PayPal at 27, becoming CFO at 28, leading the IPO at 28, joining Sequoia at 30) all came after age 26. By 26, he was an MBA student at Stanford with strong academic credentials but no founding, product, publication, or commercial success. His grandfather's political prominence provided family status but not in the technology domain.

name: Max Rafael Levchin
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Fieldlink (later Confinity, then PayPal) with Peter Thiel in 1998 at age 23, serving as CTO and building the anti-fraud systems including one of the first commercial CAPTCHAs; PayPal went public in February 2002 at age 26 and was acquired by eBay later that year.
early_history_summary: Levchin immigrated from Kyiv to Chicago in 1991 at age 16 with his Ukrainian-Jewish family and limited financial resources. He studied computer science at the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign, founding several small startups including SponsorNet New Media while still a student. In 1998, he co-founded Fieldlink (later Confinity, then PayPal) with Peter Thiel, serving as CTO. He co-created the Gausebeck-Levchin test, one of the first commercial CAPTCHAs. PayPal went public in February 2002 and was acquired by eBay in July 2002.
family_context_summary: Born in Kyiv, Ukrainian SSR, to a Ukrainian-Jewish family. Immigrated to the United States in 1991 at age 16 with limited financial resources, settling in Chicago. Had respiratory problems as a child; doctors doubted his chance of living. Took up the clarinet to expand lung capacity with guidance from his grandmother and parents.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; family was not in the technology domain. Immigrated with just a few hundred dollars.
primary_early_advantage_tags: immigrant, Soviet Ukraine, UIUC, Peter Thiel, PayPal Mafia, adversity, CAPTCHA, anti-fraud, self-created
evidence_summary: Levchin immigrated from Kyiv to Chicago in 1991 at age 16 with his Ukrainian-Jewish family and limited financial resources. He studied CS at the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign, founding several small startups including SponsorNet New Media while still a student. In 1998 at age 23, he co-founded Fieldlink (later Confinity/PayPal) with Peter Thiel, serving as CTO and building anti-fraud systems including one of the first commercial CAPTCHAs. PayPal went public in February 2002 when Levchin was 26 and was acquired by eBay later that year. His primary leverage was scarce technical depth in security and cryptography, combined with a high-trust peer team (Thiel, fellow UIUC graduates) and the adversity-driven urgency of an immigrant building from scratch with minimal resources.
